LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
 <security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD's top-level/global scope contains only variable assignments (pkgname, pkgver, pkgrel, pkgdesc, arch, url, license, depends, optdepends, source, sha256sums) followed by a definition of the `package()` function. No commands in the global scope download, execute, or exfiltrate data, and no top-level command substitution, `eval`, `curl`, `wget`, `base64`, or similar constructs are present.

The `package()` function body is not executed by `makepkg --printsrcinfo`; it will only run during a later packaging step. The source URL and checksum are ordinary metadata for the narrow gate, and a skipped or missing checksum would not matter here because no sources are fetched during this step. Sourcing this PKGBUILD for metadata printing is safe.
</details>
<evidence></evidence>
<summary>No top-level malicious code; only metadata and a function definition execute.</summary>
</security_assessment>

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD for the `mpf3` package follows standard Arch Linux packaging practices. The source is fetched from the project's own upstream website (penguiner.eu), and a sha256 checksum is provided (not SKIP). The `package()` function performs routine installation tasks: copying Python source files, assets, icons, documentation, and creating a simple launcher script and `.desktop` entry via heredocs. The heredoc content for both the launcher and desktop file is straightforward and benign — the launcher simply execs the main Python GTK application. There are no signs of obfuscated code, suspicious network requests, data exfiltration, or execution of untrusted downloaded content. No dangerous commands (eval, curl|bash, etc.) are used in unexpected contexts.
</details>

All dependencies are legitimate system packages. There is no evidence of injected malicious code, data exfiltration, backdoors, or execution of attacker-controlled code. The content is consistent with ordinary AUR packaging practices.
</details>

Therefore, running `makepkg --printsrcinfo` (which sources the PKGBUILD's global scope) does not execute any malicious code.
</details>
